hints: Focus on what the yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine really tells you, it is the iodoform test for a very specific group.
Check each alcohol for a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit, only those with this group can give the yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate.
Remember Fehling's means Z must be an aldehyde, so Y must also contain a primary alcohol group that can oxidise to $\text{-CHO}$ without being a secondary alcohol.
walkthrough:
**Decode the iodoform test**

Y gives a yellow precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine. That is the triiodomethane ($\text{CHI}_3$) test.

For an alcohol, positive result means:
$$\text{Y must contain the group } \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$$

**Decode the Fehling's test**

Z gives a red-brown precipitate with Fehling's solution. That means Z is an aldehyde.

Key rule:
$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone (no Fehling's)}$$

**Combine both clues to find Y**

So Y must have two features at once. It needs $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ for the iodoform test, and it needs a $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ primary alcohol group so oxidation can make an aldehyde.

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{OH}$ has both. Oxidation of the primary end gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO}$, an aldehyde that gives Fehling's positive result.

options.A: Contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ so it gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline iodine. It also contains a primary $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group which oxidises to an aldehyde, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO}$, and aldehydes give the red-brown $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate with Fehling's. Both tests are satisfied.
options.B: Structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It has a tertiary alcohol and a primary alcohol, but no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so it fails the iodoform test. Students sometimes see the $\text{CH}_3\text{C}$ and $\text{OH}$ and assume it is positive, but the carbon with OH must also have a H.
options.C: Structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. It does contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ so iodoform is positive, but both OH groups are secondary. Oxidation gives ketones only, which do not react with Fehling's, so no aldehyde Z can form.
options.D: Structure is $\text{CH}_2\text{(OH)CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The secondary alcohol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)}-$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so it is iodoform negative. Although the primary $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ could oxidise to an aldehyde, it fails the first test, so it cannot be Y.
